== Ingredients ==
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] plain [[Cookbook:Yogurt|yogurt]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] (240 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) water
* 1–2 [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumbers]], diced (diced is far better than grated, although at many restaurants they grate them) 
* A couple of spoonfuls [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Dill|dill]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]], to taste 
* [[Cookbook:Vinegar|Vinegar]], to taste 
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]], to taste 
* A couple of spoonfuls chopped [[Cookbook:Walnut|walnuts]] (optional) 

== Procedure ==
# Mix all the ingredients, using enough water so the soup is about the consistency of milk
# Serve cold in a soup dish, adding a couple ice cubes if it's not cold.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* If you use all of the above ingredients without the water and strain the yogurt until it becomes half in volume, you can make a salad. It is referred to as ''snezhanka'' (Snow White) or ''mlechna salata'' (yogurt salad). The main difference is that people traditionally use pickles/gherkins for ''snezhanka'' and fresh cucumbers for ''mlechna salata''.
